sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech
themes: Indonesia's energy transition hinges on PLN's capex cycle and feed-in tariff revisions, making policy clarity the dominant swing factor for local renewables valuations.
US solar demand is structurally supported by IRA subsidies and grid-scale backlog, insulating SEDG/ENPH from near-term rate volatility.
Climate-tech capital is bifurcating: US equipment makers benefit from reshoring incentives, while Indonesian developers face currency and offtake risks that cap upside.
sectors.ai: US-listed renewables rebounded on rate-cut hopes while Indonesian names lagged on rupiah weakness and policy uncertainty. Buy US solar equipment (SEDG, ENPH) for near-term beta, but rotate into Indonesian utilities (HGII) only after clarity on PLN procurement and tariff reform. Hedge IDR exposure via NRG-style cash-flow names.

sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG
themes: Mid-cap consumer names are decoupling from large-cap staples, driven by company-specific earnings beats and new product cycles, creating alpha opportunities in a flat index.
IDR volatility and imported input costs are compressing margins for FMCG players reliant on raw material imports, favoring local-sourcing champions with pricing power.
Structural shift toward premiumization and health-conscious products persists, with smaller players like POLU and AGAR capturing share from legacy brands via digital distribution.
sectors.ai: Buy selective mid-cap consumer names with idiosyncratic catalysts (BIKE, POLU, AGAR) despite sector-wide softness; aggregate weakness is rotation, not fundamentals. Trim large-cap staples exposed to IDR depreciation and weak rural demand. Watch for BI rate cuts in H2 to re-rate domestic discretionary.
